items.stem: Electricity is best described as which of the following?

options.text: A type of metal found inside wires
A liquid that flows out of outlets
A form of energy carried by electric charges
A kind of light that only appears at night

items.explanation: Electricity is a form of energy made up of electric charges. Those charges can produce light, heat, or motion.

items.stem: Which of these is an example of static electricity?

options.text: A spark when you touch a doorknob after walking on carpet
A lamp glowing while plugged into the wall
A refrigerator running in the kitchen
A phone charging overnight

items.explanation: A doorknob spark is static electricity: charge that builds up on a surface and then discharges. The lamp, refrigerator, and charging phone all use current electricity.

items.stem: What is the main difference between static and current electricity?

options.text: Static electricity can only happen during a thunderstorm outdoors
Static charge builds up and stays, while current is charge that flows
Current electricity cannot do any useful work
They are two names for the exact same thing

items.explanation: Static electricity is charge that collects and builds up on a surface. Current electricity is charge that flows through a conductor such as wire.

items.stem: In an atom, where are the protons and neutrons found?

options.text: Orbiting far outside the atom
Spread evenly throughout the whole atom
Only on the surface of the atom
Packed together in the nucleus

items.explanation: Protons and neutrons sit together in the nucleus at the center of the atom. Electrons orbit around the outside.

items.stem: Which particle in an atom carries a negative charge?

options.text: The proton
The neutron
The electron
The nucleus

items.explanation: The electron has a charge of -1, making it negative. The proton is positive, and the neutron has no charge.

items.stem: An atom gains extra electrons. What is its overall charge now?

options.text: Negative
Positive
Still neutral
It has no charge at all

items.explanation: Electrons are negative. Gaining electrons gives the atom more negatives than positives, so its overall charge is negative.

items.stem: Two objects both have a negative charge. What will the electric force between them do?

options.text: Pull them together
Push them apart
Have no effect at all
Turn one of them positive

items.explanation: Like charges repel. Two negative objects push away from each other.

items.stem: According to the law of electric charges, which pair of objects will attract each other?

options.text: Two positive objects pushed close together
Two negative objects side by side
Two objects that both have no charge
A positive object and a negative object

items.explanation: Opposite charges attract. A positive object and a negative object pull toward each other, while like charges repel.

items.stem: How does increasing the amount of charge on two objects affect the electric force between them?

options.text: It makes the force weaker
It has no effect on the force
It makes the force stronger
It reverses the direction of the force

items.explanation: The larger the charge on the objects, the stronger the electric force between them. Distance matters too: the closer they are, the stronger the force.

items.stem: A spark jumps between your hand and a doorknob just before you touch it. What does this show?

options.text: Electricity can only move when two objects are touching tightly
Charged objects can push or pull across a gap, with no contact
The doorknob magically created brand new electrons
Static electricity is not real

items.explanation: The spark crosses the air gap, so charged objects exert a force on each other even when they are not in contact. Lightning is the same effect on a giant scale.
